entries.name: const_one_item_type-errored#0
entries.script: sigmaProp(c._1 == 1) where c is a CONSTANT of type `(Int)` — a one-item tuple TYPE, which the JVM parses and can never write back  // parses; eval fails — toDslTuple returns a raw Coll[Any] for a non-pair

entries.name: const_zero_item_type-errored#1
entries.script: sigmaProp(c == c) where c is a CONSTANT of type `()` — a zero-item tuple TYPE, whose data occupies no bytes at all  // parses; eval fails — toDslTuple returns a raw Coll[Any] for a non-pair

entries.name: tuple_expr_one_item-errored#2
entries.script: sigmaProp(Tuple(1)._1 == 1) — a one-item tuple EXPRESSION. `TupleSerializer` writes a count and no type, so this round-trips verbatim; `Tuple.eval` then refuses it  // parses and round-trips; Tuple.eval refuses any count but two

entries.name: tuple_expr_zero_item-errored#3
entries.script: sigmaProp(Tuple() == Tuple()) — a zero-item tuple EXPRESSION on both sides of an EQ  // parses and round-trips; Tuple.eval refuses any count but two

entries.name: tuple_expr_127_items-errored#4
entries.script: sigmaProp(Tuple(1 x 127)._1 == 1) — the LARGEST script tuple a signed count can express. The byte is 0x7f; one more wraps negative  // parses and round-trips; Tuple.eval refuses any count but two

entries.name: tuple_expr_128_items-errored#5
entries.script: sigmaProp(Tuple(1 x 128)._1 == 1) — one past the boundary. The count byte 0x80 reads as -128 and `safeNewArray` bounds only the upper end, so the parse throws NegativeArraySizeException and takes the whole carrier with it  // the PARSE throws: the count byte 0x80 reads as -128

entries.name: const_pair_type_control-accept#6
entries.script: sigmaProp(c._1 == 1) where c is a `(Int,Int)` CONSTANT — the writable twin of `const_one_item_type`, identical in shape  // the writable twin, and the cost baseline

entries.name: const_pair_eq_control-accept#7
entries.script: sigmaProp(c == c) where c is a `(Int,Int)` CONSTANT — the writable twin of `const_zero_item_type`  // the writable twin, and the cost baseline

entries.name: tuple_expr_two_items_control-accept#8
entries.script: sigmaProp(Tuple(1, 1)._1 == 1) — the writable twin of the expression rows, and the one count `Tuple.eval` accepts, so this is the only row of the family that also SPENDS  // the writable twin, and the cost baseline

entries.name: const_one_item_type_eq_self-errored#9
entries.script: sigmaProp(c == c) where c is a CONSTANT of type `(Int)`  // `Unsupported tuple type (SInt$)`, where the `()` twin says `Unsupported tuple type ()` — the arity of the type is what equality refuses, not its emptiness
